items.question: How many PTO days do full-time employees accrue per month?
items.answer: Full-time employees accrue PTO at a rate of 1.67 days per month (20 days per year), starting on their first day of employment [S1]. After 5 years of continuous service, the accrual rate increases to 2.08 days per month (25 days per year) [S1]. Part-time employees accrue PTO pro rata to their scheduled hours [S1].

items.question: How many unused PTO days can be carried over to the next year, and by when must they be used?
items.answer: Employees may carry over a maximum of 5 unused PTO days into the next calendar year [S1]. Carried-over days must be used by March 31 of the following year; any carried-over days not used by that date are forfeited [S1]. Employees receive 10 paid sick days per year, which do not carry over [S2].

items.question: How many days per week can employees work remotely under the hybrid policy?
items.answer: Employees may work remotely up to 3 days per week; the remaining days are spent in the assigned office [S1]. Working from another country for more than 20 working days in a calendar year requires prior approval because of tax and immigration implications [S2]. Helios operates a hybrid model [S1].

items.question: What is the maximum reimbursable amount per person for a client meal?
items.answer: Client meals are reimbursed up to $85 per person, including tax and tip, and the attendees and business purpose must be recorded [S1]. Alcohol is reimbursable only at client meals and in moderation [S1]. Team meals require director pre-approval and are capped at $50 per person [S1].

items.question: What is the deadline for submitting expense reports?
items.answer: Business expenses must be submitted in the Ledger expense tool within 30 days of the date the expense was incurred [S1]. General expense rules (submission deadline, receipts, approvals) are in the Employee Handbook [S2]. Expenses submitted after 30 days require director approval and expenses older than 90 days are not reimbursed [S1].

items.question: What is the minimum password length required by the security policy?
items.answer: Report it to the Service Desk within 1 hour so the device can be locked and wiped, as required by the Information Security Policy [S3]. Sharing Restricted data with a third party requires a signed data processing agreement and Security approval [S2]. Anything else requires a software request, which Security reviews within 3 business days [S3].

items.question: What type of MFA is required for administrator accounts?
items.answer: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for every account that accesses company systems, including email, source control, cloud consoles, the fleet management portal and VPN [S1]. Administrator and other privileged accounts must use phishing-resistant FIDO2 hardware security keys; two keys are issued per administrator, one kept as a backup in a secure location [S1]. Helios IT Service Desk FAQ The IT Service Desk supports employees with laptops, accounts, software and office equipment [S2].

items.question: How often must API keys and service-account credentials be rotated?
items.answer: API keys, service-account credentials and other application secrets must be rotated at least every 90 days, and immediately on suspected exposure [S1]. Customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) are rotated automatically every 365 days [S1]. SSH keys for production access are short-lived certificates valid for 12 hours [S1].

items.question: What are the four data classification levels and which one covers customer PII?
items.answer: All Helios data is classified into one of four levels [S1]. The data owner assigns the classification [S1]. Restricted — Highest sensitivity; legal or safety impact if disclosed — Customer PII, robot telemetry tied to a customer, firmware signing keys, pre-release financial results [S1].

items.question: What is the acknowledgement SLA for a SEV2 incident?
items.answer: A blameless postmortem is required for every SEV1 and SEV2 incident, and optional for SEV3 [S3]. Appoint roles for SEV1 and SEV2: Incident Commander, Communications Lead, Operations Lead [S4]. If the primary does not acknowledge within 10 minutes, the page escalates automatically to the secondary; after 20 minutes without acknowledgement it escalates to the engineering manager [S1].

items.question: Within how many days must a postmortem be published after a SEV1 incident?
items.answer: The postmortem draft must be published within 5 business days of resolution and reviewed in the weekly reliability review [S1]. A blameless postmortem is required for every SEV1 and SEV2 incident, and optional for SEV3 [S1]. Every action item must have an owner and a due date; SEV1 action items are due within 30 days [S1].

items.question: What is the maximum payload and battery runtime of the Atlas AMR?
items.answer: The Atlas AMR battery is covered separately for 36 months or 2,000 charge cycles, whichever comes first [S2]. Maximum payload: 150 kg [S1]. Battery: LiFePO4, 10 hours of typical runtime per charge [S1].

items.question: How long is the standard warranty on the Orion Arm?
items.answer: Product — Standard warranty [S1]. Orion Arm — 18 months [S1]. Helios sells four products: the Atlas AMR autonomous mobile robot, the Orion Arm collaborative robot arm, the Vega Vision Kit perception module, and the Nova Controller edge compute unit [S3].

items.question: When is business class allowed for flights?
items.answer: Flights over 10 hours of scheduled flight time: business class is allowed [S1]. Business class on shorter flights requires written approval from a Vice President [S1]. Flights with a scheduled flight time under 6 hours: economy class [S1].

items.question: What is the daily meals per diem in Tier 1 cities?
items.answer: City tier — Example cities — Meals per diem (USD/day) — Hotel cap (USD/night) [S1]. Meals and incidentals are reimbursed as a daily per diem; receipts are not required for per diem [S1]. Tier 1 — New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich, Tokyo, Singapore — $95 — $350 [S1].

items.question: How long is raw robot telemetry retained?
items.answer: Raw robot telemetry (sensor logs, trajectories and camera snapshots) is retained for 18 months from collection [S1]. Restricted — Highest sensitivity; legal or safety impact if disclosed — Customer PII, robot telemetry tied to a customer, firmware signing keys, pre-release financial results [S3]. After 18 months telemetry is aggregated and anonymised; anonymised aggregates may be kept indefinitely for product improvement [S1].

items.question: How long are production database backups retained?
items.answer: Production database backups are retained for 35 days [S1]. Monthly snapshots used for disaster recovery testing are retained for 12 months [S1]. Helios keeps data only as long as needed for business, legal and safety purposes [S2].

items.question: Which Helios OS release added single sign-on support?
items.answer: Single sign-on (SSO) for Helios Cloud via SAML 2.0 and OIDC, with SCIM user provisioning [S1]. Mission scheduler supports time-window constraints for pick-up and drop-off [S1]. Helios OS runs on every Helios robot and on Helios Cloud [S2].

items.question: How often are company laptops replaced?
items.answer: Helios IT Service Desk FAQ The IT Service Desk supports employees with laptops, accounts, software and office equipment [S1]. Company laptops are refreshed every 3 years [S1]. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption, the managed endpoint-protection agent and automatic OS updates enabled [S2].
